course.title: Data Structures and Algorithms — From Beginner to Advanced
course.description: A progressive, visual-first DSA course spanning problem solving, complexity, linear and nonlinear structures, searching/sorting, strings, graph algorithms, algorithm design, professional practice, projects, and advanced optional specializations. Topic numbering and source subtopics are preserved from the attached 35-page curriculum PDF.
course.version_scope: Language-independent DSA concepts; inspectable implementation examples use Python 3.12+. Official reference URLs were catalogued on 2026-10-14; verify versions, errata and implementation behavior during specialist review. Specialized topics may require additional current papers and implementations.
audience: Software developers strengthening algorithmic problem solving
Competitive-programming and algorithm-engineering learners following optional tracks
prerequisites: Basic programming knowledge helps but is not required at the beginning. Learners should gradually become comfortable with variables, conditions, loops, functions, and arrays in one programming language.
Python 3.12+ is used for code-reading examples; equivalent implementations in another language are acceptable.
learning_outcomes: Understand and implement common data structures and algorithms.
Analyze time and auxiliary-space complexity and distinguish expected, worst-case and amortized costs.
Select appropriate algorithms and data structures for search, ordering, graph, string, range-query and optimization problems.
Build correct solutions with explicit assumptions, invariants, tests and edge-case handling.
Compare baseline and improved approaches and explain practical trade-offs.
Deliver a documented DSA project with reproducible tests and a reasoned complexity report.
